# Zoning & Development Analysis: 6247 N Rockwell St, Chicago IL
**PIN:** 13012120030000 | **Parcel Resolution:** Authoritative

---

## 1. Zoning District in Effect

This parcel is zoned **RS-2** (Residential Single-Unit, Detached House District) per the City's official GIS parcel layer. RS-2 is one of three single-family detached house districts defined by [3], distinguished primarily by minimum lot area requirements and floor area ratio. You can verify the current zoning at the official Chicago Zoning Map: [https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

## 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Almost certainly not by right — and it would be very difficult.** RS-2 is a single-unit detached house district [3]. Two-flats (two dwelling units) are not a primary permitted use in RS districts; they belong principally to RT (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit) districts [3].

The one narrow exception noted in the code is in **RS-3** (not RS-2): [2] allows the minimum lot area per unit to be reduced to 1,500 sq ft in RS-3 when 60% or more of the lots on the same block face are lawfully improved with multi-unit buildings ("Predominance of the Block"), permitting a two-unit building. That exemption is explicitly written for RS-3 and **does not apply** to RS-2.

To pursue a two-flat, you would need a **zoning map amendment (rezoning)** to at minimum RT-3.5, which requires City Council approval. This is a legislative process, not an administrative one.

---

## 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards for RS-2

The retrieved code provides direct guidance on minimum lot area per unit [2] and parking location [4], but the full RS-2 dimensional table (FAR, height limits, setbacks) was not returned in the retrieved code chunks. Based on what is available:

| Standard | RS-2 Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Minimum lot area per unit** | RS-2 has its own (more restrictive) minimum lot area standard; the 1,500 sq ft reduction to allow a second unit applies only to **RS-3**, not RS-2 [2] | [2] |
| **Density** | One dwelling unit per lot (single-family only) by district purpose [3] | [3] |
| **Off-street parking location** | Prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 ft of front property line; required spaces must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling served [4] | [4] |
| **FAR, max height, setbacks** | ⚠️ *Not returned in retrieved code — see below* | — |

> **What I could not determine:** The specific FAR, maximum building height, minimum front/rear/side setback figures, and the exact minimum lot area per unit for RS-2 were **not included in the retrieved Municipal Code sections**. These are set out in the RS district tables in Chapter 17-2. You should look up §17-2-0303 (lot area per unit table) and §17-2-0400 (bulk standards table: height, FAR, setbacks) directly in the [Chicago Municipal Code](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2617) or contact the Department of Planning and Development (DPD) at (312) 744-5777.

**Your lot:** 4,125 sq ft (assessor data). This is a smaller urban lot, which will be a binding constraint on any density increase.

**ARO Zone:** This parcel falls within an Affordable Requirements Ordinance zone. The ARO primarily triggers affordable unit requirements when a developer seeks **zoning entitlements** (rezoning, PD approval, or certain city financial assistance) for residential projects. For a standard single-family project requiring no entitlements, the ARO would not be triggered. However, if you seek a rezoning to RT or RM, ARO obligations may attach. The community area (West Ridge) has 6 active ARO projects totaling 324 affordable units, including significant senior housing.

**Transit Access (Not TOD-designated):** The nearest CTA rail is the **Morse Red Line station** (~1.71 miles away) and the nearest Metra stop is **Peterson/Ridge on the Union Pacific North line** (~1.04 miles away). The parcel is **not** TOD-eligible under the Connected Communities Ordinance, so no transit-related parking reductions or density bonuses apply.

**Walkability:** The location has a Walk Score of 74/100 (Very Walkable), Transit Score of 56/100 (Good Transit), and Bike Score of 77/100 (Very Bikeable), with a Divvy station at Western Ave & Granville Ave just 0.27 miles away.

## 5. Parking Requirement and Transit-Related Reductions

In RS districts, off-street parking must be [4]:
- Located on the **same zoning lot** as the dwelling units served [4]
- **Not placed in side setbacks** or within 20 feet of the front property line (except when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front) [4]

The parcel currently has a **1-car garage** (assessor data), which satisfies the accessory parking standard for a single-family home.

**Transit reduction:** Because this parcel is **not in a designated TOD area**, no parking minimum reduction under the Connected Communities Ordinance (§17-10-0102-B) applies. The standard RS-2 parking requirements govern.

---

## 6. Coach House / ADU

**No — not permitted under current regulations as retrieved.**

A building permit for a new coach house in an RS-zoned district **may not be issued unless the lot is within a designated ADU-Allowed RS Area** [5], as defined by [1]. This parcel is confirmed **not** in an ADU-Allowed RS Area per the regulatory data.

The code sets out additional coach house standards that would apply *if* the parcel were eligible [5]:
- Maximum coach house height: **22 feet** [5]
- Rooftop features: no higher than 22 feet above grade [5]
- At least **3 feet of open, unobstructed space** between the coach house and at least one side property line for the full length of the building wall [5]
- A coach house may be established **without** accessory parking to serve itself [5]
- Parking for the principal building may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment [5]

But none of these provisions are accessible to you here because the foundational eligibility requirement — being in an ADU-Allowed RS Area
